summary: Learn to assess psychosocial risks, design controls and integrate actions into OHS systems. Explore the five-day occupational mental health course.
lede: Psychosocial risk management helps HSE, HR and occupational health professionals identify and control work-related hazards through existing OHS processes. Participants practise assessing exposure, building risk registers, choosing organisational controls for workload, violence and emotionally demanding work, and drafting policies, manager guidance and action tracking. The focus is practical workplace prevention and review using ISO 45001:2018 and ISO 45003:2021—not clinical diagnosis or treatment.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape work conditions, manage people or maintain OHS processes where psychosocial hazards need a clear owner and practical controls.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with HR, occupational health or OHS processes is recommended. No prior mental health specialty qualification or coding experience is required. The course focuses on organisational risk management, not clinical diagnosis or treatment.
